outlook: Grains were mixed in overnight trade Wednesday after Tuesday's big rally. December corn slipped about 3 cents to $5.05 and all wheat contracts eased, with Minneapolis December spring wheat down 1.5 cents to $7.18, though drone attacks on ships near Bulgaria and Romania and late U.S. winter wheat planting (36% vs. 46% average) limited the losses. November soybeans edged up 2 cents to $13.05 on slow Brazilian planting and steady U.S. export demand, while canola dipped about C$6. Harvest is still running behind normal after heavy Midwest rain, and traders are waiting on Friday's USDA WASDE and Crop Production reports; Minneapolis cash bids shown are from Tuesday's USDA report, the latest available.
